Ellen — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary and I’ve attached a short export spec and a small sample extract (redacted) for your review. Where helpful I call out differences between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Quick answers (TL;DR):
- Retention windows: default admin & system audit logs = 90 days (hosted). Configurable up to 7 years for Hosted via retention policy; Dedicated and Private support unlimited retention subject to customer storage (we’ve implemented customers at 10+ years).
- Export formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON), Parquet (columnar), and compressed tarball (gzip). Exports include per-record integrity metadata (SHA256) and a signed manifest summarizing sequence ranges and root HMAC for tamper evidence.
- Redaction/pseudonymization: three modes — (1) On-export redaction (pattern-based removal), (2) Pseudonymization with irreversible hash, (3) Reversible pseudonymization (tokenization) where reversible keys are customer-controlled via KMS (recommended for forensics). Hosted reversible mode uses customer-managed KMS (via cross-account key link) when requested; Private/Dedicated can be configured to use your on-prem/HSM keys.
- Key management: For reversible tokenization we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) using envelope encryption. Redwood does not retain plaintext reversible keys for Hosted with customer KMS configured.
- SLA / turnaround: Standard bulk export (up to 30 TB, 1–3 years of logs) = 5 business days. Expedited service (48–72 hours) available for Dedicated/Private customers and for Hosted customers on an enterprise support plan (fee-based).

Operational notes and controls:
- Exports preserve event timestamps, event type IDs, and non-PII metadata by default to keep analytic value. Full message payloads or free-text fields are redacted only when redaction rules match or upon a specific legal hold request.
- Chain-of-trust: Every export includes a signed manifest, per-file SHA256 sums, and an export provenance record that lists the applied redaction rules and KMS key identifiers. We can provide a notarized timestamp (RFC 3161) on request for legal handoffs.
- Format & schema: Attached is redwood-audit-export-spec-v1.pdf and a 5k-line sample (sample-audit-snippet.ndjson) demonstrating the schema (timestamp, actor_id, event_type, resource, payload, sha256, redaction_flags).
- Redaction review workflow: We provide a pre-export dry-run of redaction (sample subset) for you to validate rules before the bulk run. We keep the dry-run output internal until you authorize release.

Deliverables and ETA:
- Today: export spec + sample extract (attached).
- If you want a full 3-year historical export sample for your account, we can schedule a pre-export dry-run within 2 business days and the full export within 5 business days after sign-off (expedited 48–72h if prioritized).
- I’ll attach our suggested retention-hierarchy-table.csv showing recommended tiers for logs and options for legal hold.

Next steps proposed:
1) Confirm the requested time range and whether you want reversible pseudonymization (and if so, which KMS provider).
2) We’ll run a dry-run on a 7‑day sample and share redaction output for approval.
3) Upon approval we schedule the bulk extract and deliver to an agreed S3 bucket or secure transfer.

I’m looping in Ben (for export orchestration) and Marissa (for legal/presales redlines). Happy to set a quick call if you prefer.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
